Definition:
`LOGIC_SWITCH` is the routing construct of a kernel directive. The agent — as the interpreter — reads its cases top-to-bottom and acts on the FIRST whose condition holds.
Authoring rules (a switch that breaks them is a kernel defect): - Every `WHEN` condition resolves from data ALREADY in context — `sdd-state` output and the classified operator intent — never from a fact the agent would have to guess. - Cases are mutually exclusive; if two could match, the one listed first wins. - A `DEFAULT` case is mandatory, so the agent never stalls on "nothing matched". - A case body is exactly one action — normally a single `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE`.
